newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent holds firm above $19, May gas oil expires.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent holds firm above $19, May gas oil expires.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures held on to early gains on Monday in a continuation of last week's technical move higher.
June Brent was 19 cents up at $19.12 a barrel at 1227 GMT.
"It's holding up quite well above $19.00, it seems quite comfortable," said one broker.
The May gas oil contract expired at 1100 GMT at $171.75 a tonne, up $1.00 on the day. June was trading $1.50 up at $169.00 at 1228 GMT, with resistance seen at $171.00
Some traders were expected a delivery against the expired May contract of up to 500,000 tonnes.
But others believed it would be much less with positions squared in exchange for physical (EFP) deals.
Traders said that technical strength and renewed Middle East tensions were more supportive to the market than the blockade on Monday of the Sullom Voe Brent export terminal by local fishermen.
The blockade will not disrupt loadings on Monday with no tankers loading until Tuesday. "At the moment it is too early to say what impact the blockade will have," a dealer said.
The launch of new wargames in Iran in the Gulf on Sunday was potentially supportive, brokers said.
A top U.S. military commander pledged to defend the strategic Strait of Hormuz against any Iranian threat.
